자동 실행 경로

  • In the provided extracted text, there is no evidence of .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, malicious setup.py logic, PEP 517 build-hook abuse, or install-time automatic execution.
  • The commands in phew/cli/main.py require explicit user invocation such as phew run, phew bench, or phew trace. This appears to be normal console_scripts/CLI behavior, not automatic execution during installation or interpreter startup.
  • _load_module() in phew/cli/main.py loads a user-supplied Python input file via spec.loader.exec_module(mod), but this is part of the user-triggered optimization/verification workflow and is not evidence of malicious supply-chain automatic execution.

절취/전송/지속성/측면이동/은닉

  • Credential harvesting: The provided text does not show broad discovery of environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud credentials, GitHub/PyPI/npm tokens, CI/CD secrets, wallets, or similar sensitive files.

  • Staging/archive behavior: The .tar.gz entries in uv.lock are dependency sdist URLs and do not indicate malicious collection or staging of harvested files.
  • Persistence: No cron jobs, systemd units, LaunchAgents, shell profile edits, startup-folder registration, background polling loops, or similar persistence mechanisms were identified.
  • Lateral movement: No evidence of Kubernetes service-account token use, Docker socket access, cloud metadata access, GitHub Actions token theft, or workflow injection was identified.
  • Obfuscation/loader:

- phew/optimizer.py contains exec(compile(source, "<phew_emitted>", "exec"), ns), which appears to dynamically build a package-generated optimized function source (output_source) for benchmarking/verification.

- Based on the provided text, this dynamic execution is not tied to obfuscated external payload loading, credential theft, or install-time execution.

- Pre-scan hits such as mx.eval, mx.async_eval, and re.compile appear to be MLX computation evaluation, code generation, or regex usage, not malicious loader evidence.
